summary: Modern databases and data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML directly, letting users run model inference, generate embeddings, and perform semantic (vector) search using SQL or native APIs without moving data to separate ML infrastructure. Capabilities now span managed LLM access (e.g., Snowflake Cortex, BigQuery ML with Vertex AI), native vector search in operational databases (MongoDB Atlas, Databricks), and extension-based approaches (pgvector on PostgreSQL and Aurora). The vector database market is expanding rapidly, projected to reach roughly USD 17.91 billion by 2034 at a ~24% CAGR, reflecting that vector and AI-native data capabilities are becoming core enterprise requirements rather than optional add-ons.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, embeddings)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless access to hosted LLMs and embedding models directly within Snowflake via SQL and Python. It supports text generation, summarization, translation, sentiment, and RAG workflows, plus Cortex Search for semantic retrieval. The newer Snowflake Postgres offering extends Cortex-powered LLM and embedding access to Postgres applications while keeping data in place.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type with vector similarity functions, and Cortex Search provides a managed hybrid (semantic + keyword) retrieval service built in.
databases.llm_integration: Native managed access to multiple hosted LLMs (e.g., Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, and Snowflake Arctic) through Cortex functions and Cortex Analyst/Agents, no external AI infrastructure required.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing in Snowflake credits; Cortex LLM functions billed by tokens processed and Cortex Search by compute/storage for serving. Costs are on top of standard Snowflake compute and storage.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI and Gemini integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets analysts create, train, and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time series, etc.) using standard SQL. It integrates with Vertex AI to call foundation models (Gemini) for generative tasks, embeddings, and remote model inference directly from queries.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports VECTOR_SEARCH with vector indexes (e.g., IVF/TreeAH) and the ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING function for generating embeddings in SQL.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with Vertex AI remote models including Gemini for text generation, embeddings, and multimodal tasks via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and related functions.
databases.pricing_notes: Pay-as-you-go based on bytes processed/scanned or capacity slots, plus separate Vertex AI charges for remote model/LLM calls and embedding generation.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector for vector storage/search and pgai for in-database AI workflows
databases.description: Open-source PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through extensions: pgvector adds a vector data type and similarity search with HNSW and IVFFlat indexes, while pgai (from Timescale) adds SQL functions to call LLMs and generate embeddings from external providers. Together they enable RAG and semantic search directly in Postgres.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL. Vector search is provided by the pgvector extension, which must be installed and enabled; it is not part of the base database engine.
databases.llm_integration: Via the pgai extension and external provider APIs (e.g., OpenAI, Ollama, Cohere), allowing embedding generation and LLM calls from SQL; not a built-in managed LLM service.
databases.pricing_notes: PostgreSQL and pgvector/pgai are open source and free; costs come from hosting/compute and any external LLM or embedding API usage.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning (SQL-based model inference via SageMaker and Bedrock)
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you invoke machine learning models from SQL queries by integrating Aurora with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock (and Comprehend). This enables predictions, classifications, and generative AI/embedding calls directly within Aurora PostgreSQL- and MySQL-compatible databases.
databases.vector_search_notes: Aurora ML itself does not provide vector search. On Aurora PostgreSQL, vector search is available only through the pgvector extension (a third-party extension), so native vector search is not part of Aurora ML.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker-hosted models through SQL functions (e.g., aws_ml / Bedrock integration) for inference and embeddings.
databases.pricing_notes: Standard Aurora instance and I/O pricing, plus separate charges for the invoked SageMaker endpoints or Bedrock model usage.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML (in-warehouse model training and inference via SageMaker and Bedrock)
databases.description: Redshift ML allows users to create, train, and deploy ML models using SQL CREATE MODEL statements, powered by Amazon SageMaker Autopilot and other SageMaker capabilities. It also supports bring-your-own-model and generative AI via Amazon Bedrock for LLM-backed functions over warehouse data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not natively supported as a core vector-search engine. Redshift supports generating embeddings via Bedrock integration, but it does not provide a built-in dedicated vector index/search comparable to native vector databases.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock for LLM-powered SQL functions and with SageMaker for custom/foundation model inference directly from Redshift SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift compute/storage pricing plus associated SageMaker training/inference and Bedrock usage costs for model operations.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model serving, agents, fine-tuning) with Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks Mosaic AI provides a full platform for building, fine-tuning, serving, and governing ML and generative AI models, including foundation model APIs and agent frameworks. Databricks Vector Search is a managed, natively integrated vector database that syncs with Unity Catalog tables for RAG and semantic retrieval.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in managed vector database that creates and serves vector indexes tightly integrated with Delta tables and Unity Catalog governance.
databases.llm_integration: Native Mosaic AI Foundation Model APIs and Model Serving provide access to hosted and external LLMs (e.g., Llama, DBRX, and third-party models), plus fine-tuning and agent orchestration.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs) for compute, model serving, and vector search endpoints; foundation model usage billed per token or per provisioned throughput.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search for semantic and RAG workloads
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables storing embeddings alongside operational documents and performing approximate nearest-neighbor semantic search within the Atlas platform. It supports hybrid search combining vector similarity with Atlas full-text search and standard MongoDB queries for low-latency operational AI.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Vector Search is a built-in capability of Atlas, using vector index definitions and the $vectorSearch aggregation stage directly within the managed database.
databases.llm_integration: No built-in proprietary LLM; integrates via external providers and frameworks (e.g., OpenAI, LangChain, AWS Bedrock) to generate embeddings that are stored and queried in Atlas.
databases.pricing_notes: Included within Atlas cluster pricing; vector search runs on Atlas Search nodes/cluster resources, so costs scale with cluster tier, storage, and dedicated search node usage.
